extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar, covering 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022 alongside 210K figures.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.citeAs: Rohatgi et al., 2023, The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics, arXiv:2305.14996v2
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PDF documents and metadata were fetched from the ACL Anthology website via web crawlers. The dataset was linked to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) via Graph API, and ground truth topic labels for training a topic classifier were crawled from conference websites of online held CL conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Certain fields are only valid on a portion of the papers (e.g., only 16.8% have arxiv_paper_id). Full-text extraction failed mostly for papers between 2000 and 2015. In a manual assessment of 21 papers, 19 sections were missing, 25 out of 92 footnotes were missing, 28.78% (19/66) of figures were not detected, and 31.58% (24/76) of tables were not detected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ACL Anthology website (aclanthology.org), Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG), and virtual conference sites for ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, and NAACL 2021.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks) were removed. Full texts were extracted from PDF files using GROBID and structured in S2ORC-JSON format. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures. Language was automatically detected using a public language detection toolkit on titles and abstracts. Topics were predicted using a fine-tuned PLM (SPECTER).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground truth topic labels (STop dataset with 2,545 documents across 21 topics) were crawled from author submission/conference website programs from ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, and NAACL 2021. Silver topic labels for the rest of the corpus were generated using a supervised PLM-based (SPECTER) classification model.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, language detection library for java (Shuyo, 2010), SPECTER, SciBERT, BART-large-MNLI, YAKE!
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing papers recently added to the ACL Anthology, identified by monitoring changes in URLs. Future plans include providing full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology to host OCL data on ACL Anthology directly.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables observation of research trends, advances open science and reproducibility in computational linguistics, and assists in building scientific assistants or knowledge graphs, while highlighting disparities in representation across topics and languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus heavily features English with low-resource languages underrepresented. Top-cited papers show topic bias toward dominant areas like Machine Translation. Full-text extraction has tool-inherent biases and error rates varying across publication years (especially 2000-2015).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Small-scale and limited to peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology (excluding arXiv and other sources). Unlabeled resource lacking ground-truth annotations for specific tasks (topics outside the training set are silver-labeled). Formatting extraction issues with GROBID (missing sections, merged paragraphs, inline equations, misidentified captions, footnotes merged into text, missing tables/figures).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Observing temporal research and topic trends, bibliographic and metadata analysis, citation network analysis, training/fine-tuning scientific language models (e.g., Galactica, Llama), document-level information extraction, summarization, related work generation, multimodal research (figure captioning), and academic search/knowledge graph construction.
